Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. - schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. content.text:
Nothing warranted this cycle.

The premium pipeline already reads as a clean ordered composition — item-level modifiers fold into each item's base, the component-block discount applies to the policy base, and policy-level modifiers (including the first-insurance surcharge) multiply that discounted base as exact rationals before the fee is added. The surcharge required no new code and no structural seam; adding one now would be speculative abstraction against Rule 4. Naming (`quotePremium`, `policy base premium`, `HIGH_ENCHANTMENT_LEVEL`) still matches current intent, there is no duplication between the item-modifier and policy-modifier folds (they operate on different bases and the shared rational arithmetic is already extracted), and APP mass is unchanged since no code changed.

All 46 tests pass, `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.
